title: Anthropogenic host redistribution expands butterfly resource geography beyond matched-host expectations

central_claim.text: Known butterfly host identities generate substantially more anthropogenic geographic resource expansion than expected from host-species richness and plant-family composition alone; this excess is shared across taxonomic specialization classes, aligns with independent contemporary butterfly occurrences beyond structural-overlap expectations, and remains only partly realized because climate-associated filtering persists.
central_claim.support_type: global resource reconstruction + exact-count/family matched-host null + independent occurrence validation + occurrence-overlap null + independent climate cross-fit

claims.claim: Known butterfly host identities generate substantially more anthropogenic resource expansion than matched alternative hosts with the same host-species richness and plant-family composition, without a disproportionate advantage for broad family-level generalists.
claims.status: exploratory macroecological reconstruction with post-hoc matched-host null
claims.evidence: 215 host-taxonomy-lower-bound-adequate species in matched-null analysis; 239 species in full reconstruction.
claims.key_statistic: observed total added units=13,529 vs null median=8,046; mean log expansion=0.444 vs 0.291; median=0.329 vs 0.195; no randomized value as large as observed in 1,999 draws (Monte Carlo p<0.001); observed rho(host-family breadth, log expansion)=0.015 vs null median=0.004, p=0.7865
claims.phylogenetic_sensitivity: Kawahara exact-species subset n=124: Brownian rank-PGLS beta=0.140, p=0.119; Pagel lambda=0.033, beta=-0.051, p=0.581.

claims.claim: Introduced host ranges recover contemporary butterfly occurrence units lying beyond native-host geography more often than expected from structural overlap.
claims.status: independent-panel occurrence validation with post-hoc null models
claims.evidence: 32-species independent panel; 23 species with outside-native occurrence units.
claims.key_statistic: 66/115 outside-native species×WGSRPD3 units recovered (57.4%); species-level mean recovery=0.583 vs region-matched null median=0.385 with 0/99,999 exceedances; excluding Pyrgus communis leaves 44/93=47.3% vs null median 30 units with 0/99,999 exceedances

claims.claim: The apparent specialist-generalist gradient in host-contribution concentration is largely explained by structural constraints imposed by resolved host-species richness.
claims.key_statistic: raw rho=0.492/-0.486; exact-host-count-adjusted r=0.059/-0.071 with p=0.502/0.415; joint host-count+butterfly-Family r=-0.039/+0.015

claims.claim: Climate-associated filtering is common within contemporary host-resource opportunity and persists after geographic-distance controls.
claims.status: independent cross-fit descriptive result with post-hoc spatial sensitivities

claims.claim: The pre-specified prediction that broader host-family diets weaken climate filtering was not supported and remains imprecisely estimated.
claims.status: independent directional hypothesis test + post-hoc precision diagnostic
claims.key_statistic: partial rho=-0.166; one-sided p=0.2237; bootstrap 95% interval -0.583 to 0.261; approximate 80%-power MDE |rho|≈0.505

forbidden_overclaims: Introduced host distributions caused butterfly range expansion.
A recovered butterfly occurrence proves local larval use of an introduced host.
Every reconstructed introduced-host region is currently used by the butterfly.
The occurrence overlap null establishes causality.
Butterfly Family adjustment is equivalent to PGLS.
Host-family breadth has exactly zero effect on proportional expansion or climate filtering.
Climate alone determines realized butterfly distributions.
The raw specialist-generalist portfolio-concentration gradient is an independent biological mechanism.
The matched-host null proves that butterflies evolved to use globally redistributed plants.
The 32-species panel was prospectively designed as an occurrence-validation panel.

required_language.resource_geography: Use reconstructed or potential resource opportunity, not realized butterfly range.
required_language.occurrence_validation: State that the 32-species panel was originally stratified for the climate test; treat occurrence validation as an independent secondary use. Report species-cluster and leave-one-out robustness, including Pyrgus communis.
required_language.anthropogenic: Attribute resource-envelope expansion to introduced host distributions, not causal butterfly expansion.
required_language.architecture: Describe raw concentration patterns as structurally constrained and secondary.
required_language.climate: Use climate-associated filtering language, not proof of physiological causation.
required_language.negative_primary: State that the directional climate-release prediction was not supported and was imprecisely estimated, not that the effect is zero.
required_language.matched_host_null: Describe excess expansion as an association of actual host identity with introduced geography beyond matched host count/family expectations; do not infer evolutionary adaptation or causal selection for globalized hosts.
